work_orders.problem_description: During the morning shift the operator noticed a temperature-related warning on the compressor display and that the casing near the cooling area felt hotter than usual. The unit kept running and no shutdown occurred.
work_orders.initial_equipment_observation: Compressor running; temperature-related warning shown on the display (message text recorded in the request); no visible leakage; no unusual smell reported.
work_orders.initial_assessment: Possible contributing factors include restricted cooling airflow, condition of cooling surfaces or filters, lubricant level or condition, and poor ventilation around the unit. None was confirmed at assessment; inspection required. Supervisor raised priority to HIGH because of the temperature warning on a running pressurised machine.
work_orders.inspection_findings: After safe shutdown, cool-down and isolation under the Company Safety & LOTO Procedure, visual inspection found heavy dust and debris on the cooling surfaces and a visibly dirty air intake filter. Lubricant level indicator showed a normal indication per the unit's own indicator. No other abnormality was seen during the visual inspection.

safety_considerations: Hot surfaces: allow to cool before contact.
Stored pressure and electrical energy must be isolated and controlled under the Company Safety & LOTO Procedure before any cover is opened.

work_orders.maintenance_performed: Isolated and locked out; cooled; cleaned the cooling surfaces and replaced the air intake filter element following the manufacturer manual; refitted guards; removed lockout; performed an observed test run.
work_orders.root_cause: Reduced cooling effectiveness associated with accumulated dust and debris on the cooling surfaces and intake filter (supported by inspection observations). The underlying reason for the accumulation (cleaning frequency or ventilation) was not established.
work_orders.maintenance_action_performed: Cleaning of cooling surfaces and replacement of the air intake filter element per the manufacturer manual, followed by an observed test run.

work_orders.problem_description: The operator reported that delivered air pressure at the point of use was lower than usual and that the compressor seemed to run for longer periods to keep up. No alarm was displayed.
work_orders.initial_equipment_observation: Compressor running; pressure indication lower than the operator's usual observation; no alarm; faint hissing sound noticed near the piping.
work_orders.initial_assessment: Possible causes include air leakage, filter restriction, control or valve behaviour, or increased demand. None confirmed; inspection required. Rated HIGH because it involves a pressurised system and affects production air supply.
work_orders.inspection_findings: With the affected section made safe, a leak-check was carried out with an approved leak-detection method. A leak was observed at one pipe/hose fitting downstream of the compressor outlet. Gauge and display indications were consistent with each other; no other fault was found in the inspected area.

work_orders.problem_description: After a line cleaning activity, the operator noticed the conveyor belt hesitating at start-up under load and appearing to slip relative to the drive pulley, with some product delay.
work_orders.initial_equipment_observation: Conveyor running intermittently slow under load; belt appeared to move unevenly at the drive end; no unusual smell; no abnormal noise reported.
work_orders.initial_assessment: Possible causes include reduced traction at the drive pulley (for example from contamination), belt tension, belt or pulley wear, or overload. None confirmed; inspection required.
work_orders.inspection_findings: After isolation under lockout, residue and a moisture film were observed on the belt underside and the drive pulley surface. Belt tension appeared lower than the manufacturer procedure expects when checked as the manual describes. No obvious belt damage or pulley damage was observed.

work_orders.problem_description: The operator observed the belt tracking toward one side of the frame with its edge nearing the side structure, producing an intermittent contact sound.
work_orders.initial_equipment_observation: Conveyor running; belt edge visibly closer to the frame on one side; occasional light contact sound; product slightly off-centre.
work_orders.initial_assessment: Possible causes include roller or frame alignment, belt condition, loose adjustment hardware, or uneven loading. None confirmed; inspection required.
work_orders.inspection_findings: After isolation under lockout, light edge-contact marks were seen on the belt edge and an adjustment fastener near the tail end was found loose. No structural damage was observed.

work_orders.problem_description: Surface finish on a production batch deteriorated gradually toward the end of the run. The operator found the cutting tool edge visibly worn. No machine alarm occurred.
work_orders.initial_equipment_observation: Machine stopped by operator at the end of the cycle; worn cutting edge visible; no alarm; no abnormal spindle noise reported.
work_orders.initial_assessment: Tool wear is a common cause of finish deterioration, but tooling, process parameters, coolant delivery and machine condition each need checking. None confirmed.
work_orders.inspection_findings: Cutting edge worn as reported. Tool holder was clean with no visible damage. Coolant flow reached the cutting zone as expected. No abnormal sound or alarm during a controlled test run.
